shortDefinition: A small, carefully curated set of inputs with known-correct answers used as the reference standard for evaluation.
fullDefinition: A golden dataset (also called a golden set or reference set) is the ground truth you measure against. Unlike a broad benchmark, it is deliberately small and hand-checked, usually 50 to a few hundred cases, chosen to cover the situations that actually matter for your application: common queries, known-hard edge cases, and the failure you shipped last quarter. Because it is small, every case can be reviewed by a human and kept correct as the product changes. The trade-off is coverage — a golden set can be over-fitted, so it should grow over time and be supplemented with broader benchmarks. Its most valuable property is that it reflects **your** domain, not a generic academic task.
examples: 100 real customer questions with the answer a support lead approved
Every previously reported bug turned into a permanent test case
A set of 30 hard edge cases that must never regress
